spot.v: Small flying insects in the room, on shelves and sticky traps. Flies bring blotch. King oyster is hard to grow without fly problems.

look.v: Identification and biology of fungus gnats, phorid flies and mites are NOT covered in the sources.

cause.v: Open doors and gaps. Compost near entrances. Case: fungus gnats wiped out the POCNS blue oyster at Catawba (Ryan).

treat.v: Catawba's response: tape every gap, fit magnetic bug screens on every opening, hang sticky traps everywhere (about 8 per room or one per shelf). Keep compost away from entrances.

prevent.v: A coarse filter on a humidifier box intake keeps bugs out.

risk.v: King oyster; fluffy POCNS-type blue oysters were devastated at Catawba.

spot.v: Gnats and live grubs, broken grain and debris in totes; sorghum is attacked far faster than other grains, even in dry climate-controlled super sacks.

look.v: Moth-damaged sorghum bursts when cooked and can trigger stroma.

cause.v: Poor grain sources and slow turnover. Early local Maine grain was about 50% bugs and debris.

treat.v: Do not use. Ask experienced growers for good sources and ask suppliers about cleaning and grade.

prevent.v: Store grain and pellets dry, indoors, and turn the stock over fast. A grain cleaner (vacuum plus sieves) helps small growers.

risk.v: Sorghum most. Millet and feed-store bags also seen.

spot.v: Rodent-chewed sacks, droppings in feed-store bags. Rats love raw soy pellets and bore through warehouse walls for grain.

look.v: Combo pellets (sawdust and soy hulls) are ignored by rats, unlike pure soy hull pellets.

cause.v: Open stores of soy pellets and grain.

treat.v: Pest control is an ongoing war.

prevent.v: Indoor dry storage. Combo pellets for one farm meant no chewed sacks or infested batches.

name: PESTS AND MITES IN SHARED CULTURES
aka: HITCHHIKERS ON CULTURES, LOGS AND BLOCKS

spot.v: Mites or insects on shared cultures; a culture 'sometimes is not what it says it is'.

look.v: Bought-in cultures and imported logs and blocks can carry hitchhikers. Some overseas producers use formaldehyde as a cheap sterilant and many do not use autoclaves.

cause.v: Sending cultures between farms can spread viruses, insects or mites.

prevent.v: Track where every culture came from and who kept it before you. Use genetic testing when you can. Mites are named only in passing.
